Finding: Lecturer CMS/Learning Explainer tab keeps Streamlit running indicator active for ~55-60 seconds on first access in a fresh server process, with the form already visually rendered but not yet interactive-stable, and no visible loading message shown during the wait
User Impact: A Lecturer opening this tab for the first time after a deployment/restart experiences up to a minute of unresponsive-looking UI, indistinguishable from a hang
Technical Impact: Confirmed via 10 timestamped samples over 60s: one-time bounded cold-start delay (settles at t=57s), not an infinite/runaway rerun loop
Root Cause: Likely lazy first-load of a local embedding/ML library triggered by llm_integration.get_embedding() (cms_lecture_repository.py) -- same documented pattern as ai_advisor.py _ensure_local_llm_libs()
Expected Behavior: A one-time loading indicator/message during first-access model warmup, or pre-warming the embedding model at app startup instead of on first tab access
Fix: PARTIAL FIX (pre-defense hardening, 2026-09-16): root cause measured directly (not assumed) -- dss.config._ensure_local_llm_libs() (first-time import of torch/transformers/sentence-transformers, ~7-16s in a clean process, machine/disk-cache dependent) followed by SentenceTransformer(...) instantiation (~3-4s), both triggered lazily the first time any embedding-consuming feature runs. Per explicit instruction, latency itself was NOT touched at that time -- the existing @st.cache_resource caching on load_embedding_model already prevented repeat cost within a process. What changed then: cold-start spinners added everywhere (see original Fix text, preserved below). FOLLOW-UP FIX (PERF-001 pass, 2026-09-17): re-profiling with dev-only timing instrumentation (dss.config.perf_mark, gated by EDUDSS_PERF_DEBUG, never active in production) found the actual measured 60-96s cold open was NOT primarily the torch/transformers import -- it was (a) admin_reports.py:199 and ai_advisor.py:393 unconditionally calling _ensure_local_llm_libs() just to display package-installed status on pages that do not use embeddings, and (b) an unconditional per-item widget-rendering loop over 743 accumulated automated-test lesson records + 176 test quiz-queue items left in the shared dev data_warehouse/cms/*.json stores (Streamlit's st.tabs() renders every tab body on every rerun regardless of visible selection). Both root causes fixed: the two eager call sites now use the existing cheap dss_config.HF_AVAILABLE (find_spec) flag instead of forcing a real import, and the 741 test-generated lesson/quiz records were removed from the live JSON stores (2 genuine CS301 demo lessons kept; full backup retained). The underlying first-ever torch/transformers import cost for a genuinely first embedding-consuming action (asking a question) is unchanged by design -- out of scope per this pass's own stop condition (no model replacement/quantization).
Verification: Original: 10 new unit tests (message helper) + 2 new E2E tests (Learning Explainer renders without traceback). PERF-001 follow-up: full non-E2E suite re-verified 444/444 green; full E2E suite re-verified (see RELEASE_FREEZE.md for exact count); live Playwright timing before/after: Admin/Lecturer Learning Explainer cold open 60.5-96.5s -> 12.9s; warm re-open 5.1s; Student first retrieval (genuinely first-ever embedding+LLM call) 24.3-25.4s (unchanged, inherent); second retrieval (model already warm) 5.1s, confirming 0 repeat embedding-library imports via instrumentation logs. See reports/performance_optimization/PERFORMANCE_BEFORE.md and PERFORMANCE_COMPARISON.md for full measured detail.
Status: PARTIAL -- UX FIXED AND WARM PATH OPTIMIZED; FIRST PROCESS COLD IMPORT REMAINS

Finding: Dark mode metric card values/labels were nearly invisible (dark-on-dark). Root cause confirmed via live getComputedStyle(): Chromium paints text using -webkit-text-fill-color when present, which wins over color. ~40+ rules in main.css pair color:var(--text-main) with -webkit-text-fill-color:var(--text-main) or a hardcoded light-mode hex; the dark-mode CSS block in dss/config.py::inject_styles() only overrode `color`, never `-webkit-text-fill-color`.
User Impact: Admin/Lecturer/Student using dark mode could not read key metrics on the dashboard.
Technical Impact: getComputedStyle().color reported the correct light value (rgb(96,165,250)) while -webkit-text-fill-color reported rgb(15,23,42) (near-black) -- the second property is what actually renders.
Root Cause: Two parallel, incomplete dark-mode CSS implementations (a dead :root[data-theme=dark] block in main.css that nothing ever activates, and a separate hand-duplicated block in config.py that only patched `color`).
Expected Behavior: Dark mode text must be readable everywhere: light page/cards -> dark equivalents, text color always matches painted fill-color.
Fix: FIXED 2026-09-16: dark-mode block now redefines the actual semantic tokens (--text-main, --text-muted, --bg-app, --bg-surface, --border, --ed-*) at :root so the ~40 rules already reading var(...) become correct automatically, plus a single `-webkit-text-fill-color: currentColor !important` failsafe scoped to the app + sidebar neutralizing remaining hardcoded literals. ui_kit.metric_card() converted from ad-hoc inline-styled HTML to the existing .metric-card/.metric-card-label/.metric-card-value CSS classes so it participates in the token system.
Verification: New E2E test tests/e2e/test_ui_dark_mode_and_provider_health_e2e.py::test_dark_mode_metric_value_text_fill_matches_color asserts computed -webkit-text-fill-color equals computed color after enabling dark mode. Manual before/after Playwright screenshots confirm visible fix.

Finding: Sidebar section titles ("TỔNG QUAN", "DỮ LIỆU & MÔ HÌNH", "TRÍ TUỆ NHÂN TẠO", "HỆ THỐNG") were visibly clipped at the top, in both light and dark mode.
User Impact: Navigation section labels were partially unreadable, weakening visual hierarchy.
Technical Impact: Confirmed via live getBoundingClientRect(): Streamlit's own [data-testid="stElementContainer"] wrapper around the st.markdown() title call computes overflow:hidden auto with a single-line-text height estimate (~18px), but the app's larger font-size/line-height/letter-spacing uppercase Vietnamese title (with tall diacritics) needs ~30px+ -- the difference was silently scroll-clipped.
Root Cause: Streamlit's default per-element wrapper height estimate does not account for custom CSS that increases a single markdown call's rendered height.
Expected Behavior: Section title text fully visible, no clipped glyphs/diacritics.
Fix: FIXED 2026-09-16: added a `[data-testid="stSidebar"] [data-testid="stElementContainer"]:has(.dss-sidebar-group-title) { overflow: visible !important; height: auto !important; min-height: 1.6rem !important; }` override targeting exactly this wrapper.
Verification: New E2E test tests/e2e/test_ui_dark_mode_and_provider_health_e2e.py::test_sidebar_group_title_not_clipped asserts computed overflow-y is 'visible'. Manual before/after screenshots confirm all 4 section titles fully visible in both themes.

Area: Performance / Learning Explainer eager-import call sites
Finding: Two page-render code paths unconditionally called dss_config._ensure_local_llm_libs() (real import of torch/transformers/sentence-transformers, several seconds) purely to display an installed/not-installed status, on pages that never use embeddings on that render: admin_reports.py:199 (Admin home dashboard, every load) and ai_advisor.py:393 (default AI Advisor sub-tab, opened by every role).
User Impact: Every role paid a multi-second-to-tens-of-seconds one-time import cost merely by opening the Admin dashboard or the AI Advisor tab, before ever touching a feature that needs embeddings -- directly contradicting the architectural intent that only embedding-consuming features should trigger the heavy import.
Technical Impact: Confirmed via dev-only timing instrumentation (dss_config.perf_mark, gated by EDUDSS_PERF_DEBUG, never active in production) and repo-wide grep for all _ensure_local_llm_libs() call sites.
Root Cause: Both call sites only needed a package-installed check (already available for free via the module-level dss_config.HF_AVAILABLE find_spec flag, set at import time with no real import cost) but called the expensive verified-import function instead.
Expected Behavior: Package-installed status display uses the cheap flag; the real import only happens lazily when an embedding-consuming action is actually invoked (core/models.py:708/1116, both already correctly gated).
Fix: FIXED 2026-09-17: removed both unconditional calls. admin_reports.py now shows 'Da cai (da xac minh)' vs 'Da cai (chua xac minh)' depending on whether _local_llm_libs_loaded is already True elsewhere in the process (same 'configured vs verified' honesty pattern already established for LLM provider health in UI-AISTATUS-001), never forcing the import itself. ai_advisor.py's provider-list construction now uses the same cheap flag directly, with a comment explaining call_ai_provider()/load_embedding_model() already self-trigger the real import when actually needed.
Verification: Full non-E2E suite re-verified 444/444 green; full E2E suite re-verified (see RELEASE_FREEZE.md); live Playwright timing confirms Admin Dashboard and AI Advisor tab opens no longer pay the import cost unless it was already paid elsewhere in the process. See reports/performance_optimization/PERFORMANCE_BEFORE.md.

Area: Test Hygiene / CMS data store pollution
Finding: data_warehouse/cms/lessons_registry.json (shared by the live dev server and the automated pytest/Playwright suites) had accumulated 743 lesson records and data_warehouse/cms/quiz_review_queue.json had accumulated 176 quiz-queue items from automated test runs across this session, none of which were ever cleaned up after their tests completed (742/743 lesson course_ids were literally TEST_COURSE_*/GOV_COURSE_*/GOV_ML_*/GOV_HIST_*, dated 2026-09-12). Root cause (confirmed 2026-09-17): every mutable store in the app (CMS lesson registry, quiz queue, interaction log, misconception records, users.json, ai_default_provider.json, subscription.json, ai_token_usage.json, technical logs, LocalVectorStore, DataWarehouse dataset/model/training-history directories, RealConnectorLMSRepository's SQLite db) resolved its path via a module-level constant computed once at import time (Path(__file__)-relative or a bare 'data_warehouse' string relative to process CWD) -- there was no way for any test to redirect these writes elsewhere, and the 2 pre-existing opt-in isolation fixtures (isolated_users_file, isolated_default_provider_file) covered only 2 of the ~13 real stores and were opt-in per-test, not automatic.
User Impact: Opening the Admin/Lecturer Learning Explainer tab rendered full management UI (containers, checkboxes, expanders) for all 743 lessons and a full review-queue UI (per-question edit fields) for all 176 quiz items on every single page load, regardless of which CMS sub-tab was actually visible -- because Streamlit's st.tabs() executes every tab body on every rerun. This was the dominant real cost (est. 50-85s of the observed 60-96s cold open), not an ML/embedding issue at all.
Technical Impact: Confirmed via dev-only timing instrumentation showing list_lessons()/list_pending_quizzes() themselves completed in under 0.05s even at full volume, while the per-item widget-rendering loop immediately after them was unbounded; confirmed via direct inspection that course_ids were auto-generated UUIDs from this session's own test fixtures, not real content. Root-cause audit: repo-wide grep for every Path(__file__)-relative data_warehouse reference and every relative 'data_warehouse' string default, cross-checked against every json.dump/np.save/sqlite3.connect call site in dss/.
Root Cause: Automated tests (tests/test_learning_explainer_acceptance.py and others) call cms_lecture_repository.ingest_lecture_material() against the real, shared JSON-backed store with no teardown/cleanup step, so every test run permanently added new records to the same file the manual dev server reads. E2E made it worse: the Streamlit subprocess spawned by tests/e2e/conftest.py::base_url() inherited the pytest process's own environment with no override, so even a fully-isolated pytest process still drove a SERVER that wrote to the real store via the browser.
Affected Files: dss/core/data_root.py (NEW); dss/services/cms_lecture_repository.py; dss/services/learning_explainer.py; dss/services/auth_service.py; dss/services/admin_ai_config.py; dss/services/subscription_service.py; dss/services/token_tracker.py; dss/services/vector_store.py; dss/services/lms_connector.py; dss/core/warehouse.py; dss/core/logging_config.py; tests/conftest.py; tests/e2e/conftest.py; tests/test_data_isolation.py (NEW); tests/e2e/test_data_isolation_e2e.py (NEW); tests/e2e/test_kb_delete_and_coldstart_e2e.py (seeded_kb_document + 2 test bodies)
Expected Behavior: Test-generated records should never reach the shared dev data store at all -- isolation must happen BEFORE writes occur, not via after-the-fact prefix-based deletion. A fresh dev server should always reflect only real/demo content.
Fix: FIXED 2026-09-17: new dss/core/data_root.py::get_data_root() is the single centralized resolver (returns EDUDSS_DATA_ROOT if set, else the real data_warehouse/ -- default behavior for real users is byte-for-byte unchanged). All ~13 mutable stores now call get_data_root() AT THE POINT OF USE (converted from module-level constants to functions / lazy-evaluated __init__ defaults) so setting the env var late is always honored, with no scattered 'if pytest'/'if TEST_COURSE' guards anywhere in application code (Section 4 requirement). tests/conftest.py adds an autouse, session-scoped fixture that sets EDUDSS_DATA_ROOT to a fresh temp dir before the first test, PLUS a permanent pollution-guard fixture (Section 14) that snapshots the real data_warehouse/ (specific JSON file hashes + directory file listings) before the session and asserts byte-for-byte equality after -- fails the whole suite by name of the exact store touched if PERF-002 ever recurs. tests/e2e/conftest.py's base_url() now creates ITS OWN separate temp dir and passes EDUDSS_DATA_ROOT via subprocess.Popen(env=...) to the spawned Streamlit subprocess specifically (previously inherited the parent's env with no override at all) -- this was the deeper of the two gaps, since it means E2E is isolated at the SERVER level, not just the test-runner level. The 741 pre-existing test-fixture records were removed once more from the live store (same category already approved: TEST_COURSE_*/GOV_*, 2 genuine CS301 lessons kept, full backup retained) since the fix was developed and verified against them before the isolation mechanism landed.
Verification: 6 new unit tests (tests/test_data_isolation.py): env-var resolution defaults to the real path when unset (proves no behavior change for real users) and to the override when set, a real cms_lecture_repository write proven to land in the isolated root and never leak into the real lessons_registry.json, same proof for auth_service's users.json, DataWarehouse() defaulting into the isolated root, and a check that the autouse isolation fixture is actually active for the session. 1 new E2E test (tests/e2e/test_data_isolation_e2e.py) proves the SPAWNED SUBPROCESS itself (not just pytest) writes an auto-provisioned Sinh vien account into its own isolated root and never into the real users.json. Section 9 'prove isolation' executed literally: real data_warehouse/ snapshotted (CMS lesson/quiz/interaction/misconception counts, dataset/model/training-history/vector-store file listings, users.json hash) before and after the full non-E2E suite (450/450 passing) -- snapshots compared byte-for-byte IDENTICAL. Full E2E suite (39/39, including the new isolation test) passed clean with the session-wide pollution guard green (no concurrent manual server activity during the verified run). Section 11 smoke-check: real dev server started with no EDUDSS_DATA_ROOT override, confirmed login, Admin home, Model Registry, and Learning Explainer all render normally and still show the genuine CS301/K-Means demo lesson -- normal application behavior is unchanged. Section 12 re-measurement: Admin/Lecturer Learning Explainer cold open 13.1s, warm re-open 5.2s -- unchanged from the PERF-001 fix, confirming the isolation refactor introduced no performance regression.
